title: A Perpetual Motion Machine for Returns
coreMove: Treat overhead, local authority, and capital reserves as one compounding system instead of three separate management choices.
sourcePressure: Tom Murphy and Capital Cities Broadcasting show how a smaller broadcaster compounded by joining lean headquarters, local operating responsibility, disciplined capital allocation, and patience for the rare major bet such as ABC.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Do not turn Murphy into a generic lean-management hero; force every scene to show central cost, local authority, and capital optionality working together.

sourceAnchors.name: Tom Murphy
sourceAnchors.detail: The source sidecar identifies Chapter 1 as Tom Murphy and Capital Cities Broadcasting, with disciplined capital allocation, lean headquarters, decentralization, and patience around major bets.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Tom Murphy made a smaller broadcaster dangerous by keeping the center light enough that cash and judgment could keep moving.

sourceAnchors.name: Dan Burke
sourceAnchors.detail: The source sidecar says reputable support confirms Capital Cities developed a reputation for efficient management under Murphy and Dan Burke.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Murphy and Dan Burke made efficiency feel less like trimming and more like a whole operating posture.

sourceAnchors.name: Capital Cities acquisition of ABC
sourceAnchors.detail: The source sidecar supports the later Capital Cities acquisition of ABC as a surprising scale reversal and visible payoff to management quality.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The ABC acquisition lands as the visible end of a long compounding machine, not as a lucky lunge.

hook: A small company can beat a big one
counterintuition: Cost cutting creates value by itself
examples: student newspaper bottleneck reused from legacy draft
any scene built around a coffee mug or whiteboard

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: No more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'.
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: At least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person direct address, retrospective, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human.
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.domain: regional ambulance dispatch authority redesigning approval thresholds
exampleSpecs.audience: an operations director whose station chiefs wait for headquarters on routine equipment swaps
exampleSpecs.stakes: ambulance downtime rising before the winter call spike
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Sarah circles three routine approvals on the maintenance log, removes headquarters signoff below a fixed dollar threshold, and reserves her own review for exceptions that change safety or capital risk.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a laminated ambulance maintenance log clipped to a metal dispatch desk

exampleSpecs.domain: independent radio network merging three local ad-sales teams
exampleSpecs.audience: a station manager with too many central scripts slowing local sellers
exampleSpecs.stakes: losing local sponsors to a larger national chain
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Mathieu tells the central sales lead to keep only the rate floor and brand limits, then lets local managers write sponsor packages around their own market knowledge.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a torn sponsor rate card beside a mute studio microphone

exampleSpecs.domain: municipal snow-removal fleet deciding between new supervisors and plow upgrades
exampleSpecs.audience: a public works deputy trying to explain why headquarters roles will not clear roads faster
exampleSpecs.stakes: overtime overruns and delayed plow routes after the first storm
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Ingrid lays the route-delay map beside the supervisor hiring proposal and redirects the money to blade sensors that local crews can act on without another approval layer.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: salt crystals melting on the edge of a folded route map

exampleSpecs.domain: specialty bakery group choosing one oven investment over five storefront refreshes
exampleSpecs.audience: an owner with store managers pushing visible upgrades
exampleSpecs.stakes: morning wholesale orders missed because the old oven limits batch size
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: It took Marco two missed wholesale mornings to reject the cosmetic refresh list and fund the single oven that changes throughput across all shops.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a rack of half-proofed rolls waiting beside a cold oven door

exampleSpecs.domain: community theater cooperative deciding how much authority stage managers own
exampleSpecs.audience: a board chair trying to reduce chaos without centralizing every prop decision
exampleSpecs.stakes: opening night delays and a drained contingency fund
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch Anna separate safety-critical approvals from routine backstage purchases, giving stage managers spending cards while keeping the board focused on the two risks that can sink the production.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: gaffer tape stuck to a clipboard under the backstage work light

exampleSpecs.domain: Toronto lab-services startup choosing between a new executive layer and courier-routing software
exampleSpecs.audience: a founder whose investors want adult supervision at headquarters
exampleSpecs.stakes: sample pickups arriving late while cash runway tightens
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: What if the grown-up move is not a new vice president? Yusuf compares missed-pickup data with the VP salary and funds routing software plus local dispatch authority instead.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a specimen cooler with a cracked barcode label

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

skillTargets: spot when overhead is consuming capital while pretending to control it
decide when local authority improves accountability rather than loosening standards
choose a high-return operating investment over scattered visible spending
connect lean headquarters to future optionality rather than mere savings

tryThisNowSpec: Find one routine decision now routed upward and write the exact threshold that would let the closest responsible person own it while preserving one exception rule.
